sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Chartering and Operation of Offshore Platform Support Ships

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (Metropolitan France, including the continental territory, Corsica and French overseas territories as applicable under the national corporate register)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition; Unitary National Structure; legal sources including the Code de commerce, Code civil, Code monétaire et financier and European Union Regulations/Directives)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China BIT (2007) and France-China DTA (1984, as amended by the 2013 Protocol)
France-United States DTA (1994, as amended by the 2006 and 2009 Protocols)
France-Germany DTA (1959, as amended) and France-Germany BIT (1956)
Intra-EU Framework: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and EU Multilateral Arbitration Convention (90/436/EEC)
Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention)
Comprehensive network: France maintains in excess of 130 active tax treaties (DTAAs) and approximately 100 bilateral investment treaties (BITs)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier - CMF): Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50, L.561-2-2 (beneficial owner definition), L.561-45 to L.561-49 (French beneficial ownership register), R.561-1 et seq.; Decree No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 (UBO register); Code de commerce: Articles L.123-1 to L.123-33 (Trading and Companies Register - RCS), L.123-2 and L.123-3 (registration duties and Kbis); Article 1835 of the Code civil (articles of association); Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Law No. 2024-364 of 22 April 2024 (Justice 2024 law amending UBO access rules); EU Directives (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD), (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD), and Directive (EU) 2018/1673 as transposed into French law; EU Regulation 2024/1624 (6AMLD) implementation in progress; TRACFIN (Traitement du renseignement et action contre les circuits financiers clandestins) is the French FIU. The UBO register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE) is maintained electronically as a component of the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by the INPI.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_note: France does not maintain a fully public UBO register. Following the Court of Justice of the European Union judgment of 22 November 2022 (Case C-37/20, WM and Sovim), public access to the RBE was restricted. Access is granted to: (a) competent authorities (TRACFIN, tax authorities, judicial authorities); (b) AML/CFT-obligated entities (banks, notaries, accountants) filing a statutory request; and (c) persons demonstrating a 'legitimate interest' (including journalists, civil-society organizations and researchers, subject to INPI review). Nominee-shareholder arrangements are not 'friendly': directors, managers and beneficial owners failing to file the RBE declaration are subject to criminal penalties of six months' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 7,500 for natural persons and EUR 37,500 for legal persons, plus the risk of judicial prohibition of shareholding.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate shareholder (extrait du registre des sociétés étranger / certificate of good standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registrar or corporate registry of the country of origin of the parent/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the country of origin is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention) OR Consular Legalization through the French Embassy or Consulate (for non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized copy of statutory identity documents (passport or national ID card) of each ultimate beneficial owner and each natural person appointed as director (président)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identity authority of the UBO's country of citizenship / a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial certification OR Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (mandat) granted to the French incorporation agent or law firm for the filing of the RBE declaration and commercial registry formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's or shareholder's jurisdiction of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and director (recent utility invoice or bank statement, not older than 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for the initial capital contribution and chartering working-capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original letter authenticated by Hague Apostille OR bank-legalized copy for consular procedures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) of all above non-French documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-approved sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) registered on the national list (Cour d'appel) or an expert translator approved by the French authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translation certificate affixed by the sworn translator; no apostille required for the translation itself, but the underlying source document must be apostilled

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and shareholders against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists (via EU implementation); (ii) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (European External Action Service), including EU Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001 (terrorism), EU Regulation (EC) No 881/2002 (Al-Qaida/ISIL) and EU Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 (Ukraine territorial integrity); (iii) OFAC SDN List and country-specific OFAC programs (required by US correspondent banks for all USD wires); (iv) French national asset-freezing list (gel des avoirs) issued by the Direction Générale du Trésor under CMF Articles L.562-1 to L.562-18; (v) domestic 'Fiche PEF' referencing of PEP status under CMF Article L.561-10 transposing EU Directive 2015/849 Article 3(9). Enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies to this medium-risk offshore maritime charter activity, requiring source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, adverse-media monitoring, beneficial-ownership chain substantiation, and transaction monitoring for Swift Wire and Escrow Maritime payment rails. TRACFIN reporting standards apply under CMF Article L.561-15.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, operated by the INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle), in connection with the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE); name availability verification via data.inpi.fr and the Infogreffe portal (infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) of a French SAS may be expressed in any language provided it is written in Latin characters and is distinctive. Non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, CJK ideographs) must be transliterated into Latin characters for the commercial register. Under the Toubon Act (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994), the statuts, Kbis, and all mandatory corporate filings must be in French; any foreign-language terms used in the corporate name should be accompanied by a French translation in the articles of association. The name must not be confusingly similar to an existing registered company, a protected trademark (INPI), or a denomination already registered in the RNE, and must not contravene public order (ordre public) or good morals.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Banquier / Caisse de crédit (requires prior authorization from the ACPR under the Code monétaire et financier)
Assurance / Assureur / Mutuelle / Prévoyance (requires prior ACPR authorization)
République / État / Président / Ministre / Maire / Préfet / Sous-préfet / Député / Sénateur (terms suggesting public authority; prohibited or ministerial approval required)
Notaire / Avocat / Huissier / Commissaire de justice (regulated legal professions; requires admission to the relevant Bar or professional order)
Chambre de commerce / Université / Val-de-Grâce (misleading official or public-institution denominations)
Caisse d'épargne / Trésor / Sécurité sociale (public-service or social-security indicators requiring specific authorization)

Chartering / Offshore / Marine / Vessel (not prohibited per se, but subject to scrutiny for misleading commercial promise; 'Offshore' may trigger financial-marketing or licensing review depending on context)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal pre-incorporation name-reservation system; name clearance is effected at the time of registration through the Guichet Unique. The 30-day window corresponds to the recommended validity period of the supporting dossier (apostilles, sworn translations, and bank letters) pending the RNE filing. Upon rejection, the applicant receives a reasoned decision (refus d'immatriculation) from the INPI/Guichet Unique. Procedure: (1) file a rectification or substitute-name request through the same Guichet Unique portal within 15 days of the refusal; (2) where rejection is based on third-party opposition (trademark or earlier company name), attempt amicable settlement or initiate nullity/opposition proceedings before the INPI (trademark opposition) or the competent Tribunal judiciaire (commercial division); (3) where rejection arises from a prohibited or sensitive token, apply for the prior ministerial authorization (e.g., Direction Générale du Trésor, ACPR, or Ministry of Justice) before re-filing; (4) in the absence of rectification, lodge a hierarchical administrative appeal (recours hiérarchique) addressed to the Director General of INPI within two months of the refusal, and thereafter a judicial appeal before the Tribunal judiciaire (or the administrative tribunal where the refusal originates from a public authority). The RNE decision becomes final if no rectification is lodged within the procedural deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_mandate_legal_basis: Article 1835 of the Code civil and Article L.210-2 of the Code de commerce (registered office (siège social) must be stated in the articles of association and located in France); Article L.123-11-1 of the Code de commerce (domiciliation of a commercial company by a licensed domiciliation company).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible - French law allows the SAS to be domiciliated at the premises of a licensed commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) for up to five years, renewable. A virtual office is legally sufficient for incorporation and RNE registration. However, for this offshore supply-vessel chartering activity, banking acceptance for Swift Wire and Escrow Maritime rails, and the cumulative substance required for any future French tonnage-tax (Article 209-0 B of the Code général des impôts) or International French Register (RIF) filing, the presence of a physical operating office or a managed office at the vessel operator's French premises is strongly recommended. A mere letterbox address without substance would heighten the medium-risk AML profile.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 10–15% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months. French authorities (URSSAF, the tax administration via DGFiP, and TRACFIN through reporting intermediaries) do not systematically conduct unannounced inspections of newly incorporated service companies; however, the offshore-maritime sector's enhanced AML classification, the mandatory statutory license, and vessel-facing operations increase the probability of documentary due diligence and targeted verification visits, particularly where a tax-residence review or a maritime-labour (gens de mer) audit is triggered. Physical vessel inspections by the Affaires maritimes may occur separately at the chartering operation stage after incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and distinctiveness search: RNE/RNCS company-name search, INPI trademark database search and availability opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Infogreffe database access and legal-service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a single-name search in France (EUR 120–150); no statutory name-search fee is imposed by the registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, consular legalization and sworn translation bundle for UBO documents (certificate of good standing, passports, POA, bank reference letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign apostille authority, French consulate, and court-approved sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing French court tariff for sworn translations (EUR 60–100 per page) plus apostille/consular fees of EUR 30–60 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / commercial domiciliation service for the SAS (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of EUR 400–700 per annum for a standard commercial domiciliation with mail handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of French SAS articles of association (statuts), including French-language compliance, corporate-governance clauses and RBE declaration provisions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing French market benchmark for a bespoke SAS incorporation (EUR 1,800–3,500); statutory tariff not fixed by law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the mandatory incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in an approved legal-advertisement journal (journal d'annonces légales - JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales authorized by the prefecture of the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff range EUR 170–250, varying by department and company capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI / Guichet Unique registration filing fee for RNE (immatriculation au registre national des entreprises) including the UBO declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for a single SAS registration via the Guichet Unique (EUR 54 as of 2025); no additional greffe fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN/EU sanctions and adverse-media screening of UBOs, directors and counterparties (screening software and manual escalation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance data provider and French law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for a one-off medium-risk onboarding screening package (EUR 200–350)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank-account opening assistance and maritime escrow-rail readiness review (Swift Wire and Escrow Maritime) with a French or EU credit institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French avocat / corporate service provider, plus possible bank onboarding fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for legal assistance and KYC documentation coordination (EUR 250–450); bank account-opening fee, if any, charged separately by the credit institution

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10 (general company law), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-27 (SAS regime), and Décret n° 2023-436 (Guichet Unique formalities portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (operated by INPI – Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) with downstream registration at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (articles of association) together with the Déclaration de conformité et d'affectation des fonds, submitted via the M0/RCR electronic form on the INPI formalities portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for an SAS; the capital is freely determined in the articles. Cash contributions are fully subscribed and paid at formation or within the timeframe fixed by the articles, with the funds deposited into a French bank escrow/blocked account and released to the company only upon effective registration with the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — [COMPANY] SAS — [DATE]. Whereas formation of the SAS is in progress and the statutory capital has been fully subscribed, the shareholder(s) and the acting governance body RESOLVE: 1. Confirmation of the subscription and full release of the share capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] ordinary shares; 2. Adoption of the registered office at [full address], France, as the legal, administrative and tax seat; 3. Appointment of [name] as President, with the widest powers to represent the company, and of [name] as General Manager; 4. Authorization of the President to sign all formation filings, deposit funds and complete the Guichet Unique registration; 5. The registrable Kbis extract shall constitute definitive proof of incorporation vis-à-vis third parties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Clearance and Corporate Identity Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Data Centre (data.inpi.fr) and the Guichet Unique portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability request via INPI Data; conduct a formal clearance to avoid confusion with pre-existing marks or corporate names; prepare the distinguishing name wording for the SAS and verify that it is not misleading in the maritime sector. Reserve the proposed name in the draft statuts.
required_dossiers: Statutory purpose (objet social) draft referencing ISIC 5222 offshore vessel chartering
Power of attorney for any proxy acting for a foreign shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is challenged or refused by INPI, file a revised designation adding a distinctive numeric or alphanumeric element and resubmit within 3 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Statuts and Publication of the Legal Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local notary (optional, recommended for vessel charter activities) and an authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts containing the company name, form (SAS), share capital, duration (99 years), registered office, corporate object covering offshore supply vessel leasing and operation, governance rules, and share transfer restrictions. Publish a mandatory 'avis de constitution' in an approved legal gazette in the department of the registered office.
required_dossiers: Final tenure of statuts signed by all shareholders
Identity and address proofs of shareholders and officers
Certificate of the authorized JAL publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL publication is deficient, republish the corrected notice and amend the statuts by a subsequent resolution before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital into an Escrow Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French credit institution or La Banque Postale / Caisse des Dépôts holding the 'attestation de dépôt des fonds'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary French account in the name of the company in formation; transfer the full subscribed cash capital of the SAS; obtain the banker's certificate attesting the block of funds; such funds may be released only after RCS registration and shall serve as the company's opening capital.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the authorized representative
Bank KYC forms and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC on non-resident shareholders, provide notarized identity copies, and in case of rejection, re-route the deposit to another registered French credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Signature of Statuts, Declaration of Compliance and Capital Allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders, the designated President, and optionally a notary for the signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have all shareholders sign the final statuts; execute the 'déclaration de conformité' confirming compliance with statutory formation formalities; sign the 'acte d'affectation des fonds' transferring the escrowed capital to the company upon registration; appoint the President and any Director General in a first governance act.
required_dossiers: Bank attestation de dépôt des fonds
Acceptance letters of the President and Director General
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If signatures are formally deficient, cure by obtaining a rectificative act before submission to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Formation Dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI portal — formalites.entreprises.inpi.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 electronic form, attach the certified electronic copy or notarized copy of the statuts, the declaration of conformity, the capital certificate, the legal announcement publication, and identity documents of the President; pay the official filing fees; submit the dossier and track the receipt number.
required_dossiers: Statuts signed and uploaded in PDF
Identity of the President and shareholders
Ownership/control disclosure for ultimate beneficial owners (UBO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the INPI issues a 'demande de régularisation', respond within 15 calendar days through the same portal; rectify missing signatures or UBO disclosures, or the file is rejected with a new submission race.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Delivery of Kbis Extract and Official RCS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris (Registry of the Commercial Court)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon INPI validation, the registrar issues the 'extrait immatriculé' (Kbis) and allocates the RCS number; verify the SIREN, SIRET, APE code (consistent with ISIC 5222 / compatible French NAF code), and the registered office address; mark the company as legally in existence.
required_dossiers: Receipt of payment of greffe fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If discrepancies appear on the Kbis, file an immediate rectification request with the Greffe and, if necessary, proceed by court petition before the judge responsible for the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Administrative, Maritime and Insurance Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Affaires Maritimes, de la Pêche et de l'Aquaculture (DGAMPA) and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the French establishment roll (SIRET activation), open a corporate bank account in the name of the registered SAS, declare the President as the relevant legal representative for maritime personnel, register the offshore supply vessels in the French shipping register (or obtain bareboat charter-in registry consent if leasing foreign-flagged vessels), and contract P&I (Protection and Indemnity) insurance for offshore marine charter.
required_dossiers: Vessel registration documents or flag consent letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGAMPA queries vessel documentation, provide an internationally recognized classification society certificate and, if deficient, charter the vessel under a bareboat-repair regime before commercial operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Transition Écologique — Direction Générale des Affaires Maritimes, de la Pêche et de l'Aquaculture (DGAMPA) and the local Quartier des Affaires Maritimes
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Armement de navire — Permis d'armement covering offshore supply vessel operation and chartering activities under Code des transports, Book V; registration as shipping operator/affréteur for non-French-flagged chartered tonnage

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autorité Environnementale of the Inspection Générale de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable (IGEDD)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Case-by-case examination (examen au cas par cas) under Article R. 122-2 of the Code de l'Environnement; full EIA report only when the offshore vessel operations implicate exceptional maritime activity intensity in French waters or sensitive ecological zones
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL Annex I (oily water discharge ≤15 ppm via approved OWS equipment), Annex V (garbage handling), and Annex VI (SOx ≤0.10% / 0.50% sulfur cap; Mediterranean SECA sulfur limit 0.10% effective 2025), plus French inland-water/coastal discharge standards under Code de l'Environnement L. 211-1 for wastewater and hull cleaning waters; waste must be delivered to approved port reception facilities

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the shore-based registered office under French ERP regulations (5th category — simple declaration), structural load inspection not applicable to movable vessels, SOLAS safety construction certificates and safety equipment certificates for each operated offshore supply vessel, and workplace clearance issued by the Inspection du Travail Maritime for all crew accommodation and operational workspaces

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) of the French Ministry of Economy and Finance; official tax portal: https://www.impots.gouv.fr (professional 'Espace Professionnel'); business-formation one-stop shop: https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; VAT OSS/IOSS portal and Chorus Pro e-invoicing platform operated under DGFiP supervision.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Incorporate the SAS through the centralised 'Guichet Unique Électronique des Formalités des Entreprises' (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which transmits the file to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE and DGFiP; the company receives its SIREN/SIRET identifiers and its RCS registration extract (Kbis). Step 2 – Where the company has its registered office or a fixed establishment in France, the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) issues the French VAT identification number (n° de TVA intracommunautaire) automatically or upon filing of the standard registration form (CERFA n° 15954 / 'TVA 3530') pursuant to CGI Articles 286-I-2° and 287. Step 3 – A non-resident entity without a French fixed establishment must obtain a French VAT ID from the competent DGFiP non-resident unit before supplying taxable services in France and, unless the OSS/IOSS or an applicable exclusion applies, must appoint an accredited VAT fiscal representative (représentant fiscal accrédité under CGI Article 164 quinquies A) who assumes joint and several liability. Step 4 – The supporting dossier comprises: power of attorney, Kbis/extract, articles of association, evidence of the French establishment or business verification, certificate of the effective manager's residence and, for vessel leasing, the vessel registration/flag certificate and the applicable maritime charter licence (EU Regulation 852/2004 manning/flag evidence or French flag certificate).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — A French SAS is an opaque commercial company which is mandatorily subject to French corporate income tax ('impôt sur les sociétés' – IS) at entity level on all profits within its territorial scope under CGI Articles 206-1 and 209. France does not offer a pass-through/check-the-box classification: the SAS cannot be treated as a partnership or disregarded entity. The territorial scope follows the place of effective management ('siège de direction effective'); an SAS chartering offshore supply vessels worldwide remains fully within the French IS net, with the separate leveraging of tax treaties and CGI Article 209 to prevent double taxation of foreign charter income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' election; the SAS is per se entity-level taxed. The applicable statutory elections relevant to the indirect and hybrid-planning posture are: (i) formation of a single VAT taxable person ('assujetti unique') under CGI Article 267 bis, consolidating group members for VAT without merging corporate income tax positions; (ii) the election under CGI Article 269 to pay VAT on 'débits' (invoice date) instead of 'encaissements' (cash receipts), useful for long-term offshore charter hire; (iii) the limited option for small enterprises to waive VAT exemption under CGI Article 293 B IV, which is practically irrelevant for a capital-intensive SAS; (iv) the French anti-hybrid election and limitation rules under CGI Articles 212 bis and 212 quater, governing the deductibility of hybrid-financing payments and reverse-hybrid structures; and (v) the option for non-resident shareholders concerning gross-up on distributions under CGI Article 167 bis. No tax-exempt-zone election exists for mainland France: the jurisdiction is unitary and the offshore vessel charter, when managed from a French port, is automatically within the French supply-of-services rules of CGI Articles 259 A and 259 B.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.special_registration_caveat_for_offshore: For ISIC 5222 vessel leasing, the French SAS must additionally evidence its eligibility to charter vessels of French or EU/EEA flag (maritime administrative licence, crew certificates, transport document records) and must procure a separate Customs Economic Operator (AEO) status where frequent export zero-rating is claimed. Failure to maintain the statutory maritime licence triggers both transportation-law sanctions and the immediate loss of the VAT supply-of-ship classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax ('Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée' – TVA), Title II of the French General Tax Code (CGI Articles 256 et seq.), harmonised with Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: French-established taxable persons must register for VAT upon the first taxable transaction with no turnover de minimis, beyond the small-business franchise ('franchise en base de TVA', CGI Article 293 B) capped at EUR 85,000 worldwide turnover for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for supplies of services; the franchise is not accessible to a foreign-owned corporation exercising a fixed French establishment. Non-resident suppliers of distance sales of goods and electronically supplied services to French consumers become registrable once their EU-wide annual turnover exceeds EUR 10,000 (CGI Article 293 A), unless the OSS is used. A non-resident lessor supplying vessel-chartering services B2B to a French VAT-identified operator is registrable without any turnover threshold by operation of Articles 286-I and 259 A CGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured e-invoicing and e-reporting under CGI Article 289-2, with compulsory deployment as follows: large and mid-size taxpayers from 1 September 2026; small and micro enterprises from 1 September 2027. All B2B invoices must be emitted in a certified structured format (Factur-X, UBL 2.x or UN/CEFACT CII) and exchanged through either a registered commercial 'Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire' (PDP) or the State portal Chorus Pro; B2C transactions are subject to simultaneous e-reporting to DGFiP. France does not operate invoice-level fiscal stamping or pre-clearance, but the transmission occurs in near-real-time at issuance with a full audit trail (irréversibilité des données). In parallel, the offshore marine charter business is subject to the electronic customs export manifest system DELTA-X and the Entry/Exit Summary Declaration (ENS), and French-flag vessels operating from French ports must maintain continuous AIS position reporting as part of the e-regulatory evidence.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.special_rule_offshore_supply_vessel: The chartering of an offshore supply vessel (OSV) to a French-identified offshore operator is deemed supplied in France (B2B) under CGI Article 259 A unless the vessel's commercial exploitation is demonstrated to occur outside the 12-nautical-mile territorial waters or outside the French continental-shelf zone; this factual determination is decisive for applying either the French 20% rate or the 0% exemption.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (0% TVA) is available on: (A) supplies of goods physically exported to destinations outside the customs territory of the EU, under CGI Article 262-I-1°, upon conclusive proof of dispatch; and (B) the supply, leasing, hire or charter (bareboat, time or voyage) of seagoing commercial vessels used in high-seas or international maritime navigation – including offshore platform supply vessels, their crew and equipment – under CGI Article 262-II-1°/2° ('navires de commerce destinés à la navigation en haute mer' and services rendered for the needs of such vessels). To sustain the zero rating the French SAS must demonstrate: (i) the vessel is a seagoing commercial ship (French/EU-flag certificate, safe-manning licence); (ii) the charter contract and AIS logs evidence missions performed predominantly beyond French territorial waters or across international boundaries; (iii) any French-flagged cabotage element or crew-service component that remains fundamentally territorial is carved out and billed at 20%; and (iv) where the customer is a non-French taxable person, the normal B2B place-of-supply rule of Article 259 A may locate the service outside France entirely, which also achieves 0% effective taxation subject to OECD/TP documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU) filed via the DELTA-X electronic customs system together with the Exit Summary Declaration (ENS) evidencing the physical exit of the vessel/goods from the EU customs territory
Bill of Lading, Sea Waybill or a lawfully executed Charter Party containing the French port of loading, foreign port of discharge and vessel particulars
Inward Remittance Certificate or Bank SWIFT credit confirmation proving settlement of the export consideration in the agreed foreign currency
Master's declaration and continuous AIS position log for the voyage period, corroborating the high-seas or international-route operation
The commercial invoice in structured Factur-X/UBL format cross-referencing the zero-rate exemption basis (CGI Article 262-II-1°)
Vessel registration/flag certificate, EU/EEA manning licence, and the offshore operations order from the charterer for the offshore supply missions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP audit practice (Articles L. 10 and L. 13 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales) applies documentary strict-proof standards to export zero-rating. Where the export evidence is missing, inconsistent or circular, DGFiP retroactively reclassifies the supply as taxable in France, imposing: (i) interest de retard at 0.2% per month (Article 1727 CGI); (ii) a 40% penalty for bad-faith insufficiency of declared VAT (Article 1729-a CGI); (iii) an 80% penalty for documented fraud involving abusive arrangements, fictitious vessel ownership or forged transit documents (Article 1729-b CGI); and (iv) a 15% accuracy penalty under Article 1788 A CGI for material declaration errors. Criminal tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI carries up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine. In addition, the supplier is jointly and severally liable under Article 283-4 CGI for VAT not collected from the client, and the standard correction window (Article L. 169 LPF) of three years extends to ten years in fraud or dissimulation cases, allowing retrospective clawback of already-refunded export VAT with interest from the date of each payment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) acting as the national prudential supervisor; the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) exercises certain foreign exchange and balance-of-payments oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member with full capital and current account convertibility under EU Treaty provisions (TFEU Article 63). There are no binding exchange controls on foreign direct investment, trade in services, or profit remittances. However, all cross-border capital flows (including equity injections, shareholder loans, charter payments, and loan repayments) are subject to periodic statistical reporting to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments compilation. Profit remittance hurdles are generally limited to corporate tax clearance and compliance with anti-money-laundering documentation; there is no prior exchange-control authorization requirement for dividends from an SAS to a non-resident parent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation in France to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or to convert foreign currency into euros within a specified timeline. Export receipts for offshore vessel chartering may be held in foreign currency in French banks, subject to the general balance-of-payments reporting requirement (Titre V of the French Monetary and Financial Code). Reporting thresholds and timelines apply for transactions exceeding €750,000 (intra-group) or €50,000 for certain statistical declarations under Banque de France’s Regulation 2006-01, as amended. Mandatory conversion ratios are not applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Banking (CACIB)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for domestic French EMI-type fintechs (e.g., Qonto, Shine) that hold an ACPR-registered licence or an electronic money institution passport. Low for offshore digital EMIs domiciled in the UK, US, or non-EU jurisdictions due to lack of European banking licence passporting and potential breach of the French ban on unlicensed credit institution activity (Article L511-5 of the French Monetary and Financial Code). Offshore EMIs cannot open a French statutory escrow account or receive Banque de France balance-of-payments coded wire transfers without a domestic correspondent banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SAS with non-resident shareholders or offshore vessel assets, French tier-1 banks generally require physical presence of at least one statutory director (or an authorised corporate officer) for the initial onboarding KYC interview. Remote opening is permitted only in exceptional cases for established EU companies under the AMF’s digital onboarding guidance, provided biometric identity verification and video verification are used. For the chartering of offshore platform support ships, a physical board resolution and certified corporate documentation (apostilled if issued outside the EU) are required. Pure remote opening without any physical attendance is unlikely for a medium-risk maritime entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity in the offshore vessel ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified UBO registry extract (RCS / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), corporate chain chart with full ownership percentages, passport copies of all natural persons with ≥25% interest, and apostilled articles of association of each intermediate holding entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Charter counterparty located in a high-risk jurisdiction or sanctioned-flagged vessel
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Charter party contract with ISPS/MTSA compliance clauses, international Chamber of Shipping beneficial ownership declaration, sanctions screening reports (OFAC/EU/UN lists), valid vessel certificate of registry, commercial registry extracts of charterers, and proof of legitimate vessel operations under ISIC 5222.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high cross-border payment volume through the operational account relative to EBITDA
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the prior two years, forecasted cash flow plan with line-item details on charter hire, period maintenance fee schedules, dry-dock cost reserves, and tax residence certificates of all counterparties to demonstrate economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital injection from offshore tax haven entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements and wire confirmations showing the original deposit chain, tax opinion from a recognised tax advisor confirming the parent group’s substance, transfer pricing documentation under OECD Chapter II for the intercompany financing, and a declaration to the French customs and indirect taxes authority on the nature of the capital inflow.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity or shareholder-loan proceeds for the French SAS must be routed via a SWIFT MT103 message to a Euro-denominated or foreign-currency account held at a Banque de France regulated bank. The wire must include the correct balance-of-payments purpose code — for equity investment use '3100' (Foreign direct investment in France) or '3300' (Investment in French companies) where pre-2008 nomenclature applies; for shareholder loans use '3301' or '3311' depending on maturity. The bank will request a copy of the SAS’s constitutional documentation and a signed declaration from the treasurer stating the nature of the capital injection. For amounts exceeding €15,000, the bank must also submit a French customs (DGDDI/DGT) cross-border monetary declaration to the Banque de France within 20 business days. Verification includes matching the UBO and legal person identity against the ACPR’s Single Digital Register and ensuring the escrow account is segregated in the bank's books.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade disbursements is the SWIFT MT103 for unattested charter hire and operational payments, with MT700 series for documentary commercial letters of credit issued when vessel procurement or major repair contracts are settled against parallel D/A or L/C terms. For servicing a vessel master’s disbursement account (D/A) in foreign ports, a separate MT101/Multi-Cash service should be established with a correspondent network. All outbound payments must be tagged with the ECB/Eurosystem BOP code appropriate to the underlying transaction (e.g., '2001' for chartering services rendered, '2081' for vessel leasing). The bank will require a copy of the charter party, invoice, and a compliance attestation that no payments are made to sanctioned vessels under EU Regulation 269/2014.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Forward (plain vanilla deliverable forward) through a licensed French credit institution
EUR/USD Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) with an offshore counterparty if the underlying charter currency is USD and the French entity maintains EUR functional accounts
EUR/USD Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) for converting long-term USD-denominated charter receivables into EUR fixed-rate cash flows
FX rollover contracts for staggered operational disbursements in USD and NOK
Vanilla currency options (EUR put/USD call) to protect minimum USD conversion rates on quarterly charter hire

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholder approval of annual accounts (bilan, compte de résultat, annexes) and allocation of results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAS shareholders and executive president; internal corporate act, not filed with a regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the close of the fiscal year, unless the commercial court grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts may prevent the statutory accounts deposit, expose corporate officers to court-ordered convocation under penalty, and create personal liability for resulting delays and costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of approved annual accounts and supporting schedules (dépôt des comptes annuels) at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, with optional application for confidential treatment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; in practice no later than seven months after the balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 2,000 for a corporate officer and EUR 9,000 for a legal entity; court-ordered injunction to file, publication of non-compliance, and eventual administrative radiation of the RCS registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, form 2065-SD with balance sheet, profit-and-loss account and supplementary schedules) and payment of the final corporate income tax balance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal years closing on 31 December: return due by the second business day after 1 May and final tax payment by 15 May; for other closing dates: return within three months after fiscal year-end and final payment by the 15th day of the fourth month after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of net tax due after formal notice, up to 40% for habitual or bad-faith non-filing, plus late-payment interest of 0.2% per month; may trigger ex officio assessment and tax audit scrutiny

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax declaration and payment (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises) covering business premises, offices and port facilities in France
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques, local tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Form 1447-C due on the corporate income tax filing date for calendar-year entities; payment of the annual charge by 15 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty and 0.2% monthly late-payment interest; enforcement action and tax lien by the public treasury on business assets for non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner register update or confirmation (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) if shareholding transfers or ownership changes occurred during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs operated by INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or beneficial-ownership change; if no change occurs, no separate annual filing is required unless the registrar requests confirmation in connection with the accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update may expose the legal entity and its legal representatives to administrative and criminal fines up to EUR 30,000, blockage of RCS formalities, and reputational or financing consequences

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a registered statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is triggered for an SAS when at fiscal year-end the entity exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 4,000,000; net revenue EUR 8,000,000; average workforce of 50 employees. Shareholders or minority holders may require a voluntary audit, and group consolidation rules may impose additional auditor mandates.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC Regulation 2014-03); consolidated accounts, if applicable, under EU-endorsed IFRS; corporate income tax basis under the Code Général des Impôts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not administer a separate UBO confirmation statement equivalent to a UK annual return. The RBE declaration is made at registration and must be updated within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or beneficial-ownership change. Annual confirmation is integrated with the annual accounts deposit and ongoing RCS maintenance, and the legal representative must ensure that the RBE, the share transfer register, and the RCS data remain consistent and accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Share Transfer Register (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors and Corporate Officers
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 250 - EUR 700 per annum (approx. USD 270 - USD 760) for registered-office and corporate-agent services in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 4,500 - EUR 18,000 (approx. USD 4,900 - USD 19,500) for a statutory audit of an asset-heavy offshore vessel leasing SAS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. A qualifying small company may obtain a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory ownership and turnover conditions; the excess is taxed at 25%. A 3.3% social contribution may apply to companies with annual turnover of at least EUR 7.63 million and corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000, producing a marginal effective rate of approximately 25.825%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: France generally provides no broad corporate tax holiday for an SAS conducting ordinary offshore vessel chartering or operation. Available incentives may include the 15% small-company rate, the research tax credit where qualifying research is performed, participation exemption for qualifying dividends, tax consolidation, and specific maritime regimes. The French tonnage tax regime may apply to eligible shipping businesses subject to election and qualifying maritime conditions; ordinary chartering of offshore support vessels does not automatically qualify. Tax losses may generally be carried forward without time limitation, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of current-year taxable profit above EUR 1 million. A loss carryback election is generally limited to the preceding financial year and EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax authority professional portal (impots.gouv.fr espace professionnel) using EDI-TDFC or EFI where available. Form 2065 is filed with the 2058-A and 2058-B tax-result schedules, 2058-C balance-sheet allocation schedule, 2059 series schedules, and accounting schedules 2050 to 2057. Form 2572-SD is used for the corporate income tax balance payment; Forms 2571-SD, 2572-SD and 2573-SD may be used for installment and balance payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; four corporate income tax installments are generally paid annually, followed by a final balance payment. Companies with a tax liability below the statutory installment threshold may be exempt from installments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the electronic return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the return is generally due by the second business day after 1 May of the following year. The corporate income tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end, or by 15 May for a 31 December year-end. Installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, principal activity, financial year dates, tax office, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS as the taxpayer. A non-resident shareholder is not substituted for the SAS. Use the French registered office and SIREN consistently across all filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss, corporate income tax due, applicable surcharges, tax credits, installments paid and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only the French SAS tax base, including taxable French activity and properly attributed permanent-establishment or branch income where relevant. Do not exclude related-party income merely because the shareholder or lender is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss reconciled to taxable profit or loss through add-backs, deductions, exempt income, non-deductible expenses and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible interest, penalties, unsupported expenses, excessive remuneration, provisions and non-arm's-length charges. Apply French rules for depreciation, provisions, financial expenses and foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year loss, prior-year losses carried forward, losses utilized and remaining losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Track losses by year and preserve evidence of continuity of business and ownership. Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% utilization cap; separately document any carryback election.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of profit or loss between reserves, dividends, retained earnings and other appropriation categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile distributions to approved corporate resolutions, distributable reserves, withholding tax filings and shareholder-accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets, securities and other capital items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify vessel disposals, lease portfolio transfers, debt releases and related-party asset transfers under French capital-gain rules and document market valuation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation and tax treatment of short-term and long-term capital gains and losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile vessel and maritime equipment disposals to the fixed-asset register, depreciation schedules, invoices, valuation reports and accounting entries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover, value added and employee information used for tax and local-tax calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include French taxable activity and French payroll data. Vessel crews and offshore personnel require specific analysis of employment location, social-security status and permanent-establishment exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, income statement, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, receivables, payables, cash, equity and related accounting details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a complete French GAAP or permitted accounting record for the SAS. Reconcile vessel ownership, leases, deposits, charter receivables, related-party balances and foreign-currency items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income and foreign tax credits where permitted by domestic law or an applicable tax treaty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty-based credits only with proof of foreign tax paid, income attribution and treaty entitlement. Prevent duplicate relief through accounting and tax reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Specified categories of non-deductible or specially reportable expenses, including certain excessive financial and management expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report required related-party, remuneration, interest and other non-deductible categories even where the payment recipient is outside France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indirect reporting of related-party revenue, expenses, financing, management charges, royalties, guarantees and other taxable adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure consistency with transfer-pricing files, annual transfer-pricing declaration 2257-SD, country-by-country reporting and withholding tax returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax balance, credits, installments and payment account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay from an approved French or SEPA-capable account where required. Reconcile payment references with the tax account and retain payment confirmation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing filing can trigger a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% after formal notice and up to 80% in cases of fraudulent conduct or abuse. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest currently calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory exceptions. Incorrect returns may also trigger tax reassessment, interest, penalties based on intentionality, and criminal referral.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2257-SD, annual transfer-pricing declaration, filed electronically through the French tax authority professional portal. Form 2258-SD is the country-by-country report where the group meets the applicable consolidated-revenue threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 2257-SD is generally due with the corporate income tax return. The country-by-country report is generally due within 12 months after the close of the relevant reporting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, financial year, legal name, turnover and balance-sheet information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS figures and identify the ultimate parent, controlling entity and relevant foreign related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts and categories of transactions with associated enterprises, including purchases, sales, services, financing, royalties, guarantees and asset transfers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross transaction categories consistently with the general ledger, contracts, invoices and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of documentation availability and information concerning the group and foreign counterparties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain local and master files in French or an accepted language and provide them promptly upon audit request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or inaccurate filing may trigger the general tax-return penalties and a specific transfer-pricing documentation penalty. The documentation penalty can be substantial, generally based on the higher of a statutory minimum and a percentage of the corrected profits or transactions, subject to statutory caps and procedural requirements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid by a French SAS to a non-resident corporate shareholder, the domestic withholding tax rate is generally 25%, subject to treaty relief and statutory exemptions. A qualifying EU or EEA parent may obtain exemption under the French implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring minimum ownership, holding-period and subject-to-tax conditions. Dividends paid to non-resident individuals generally have a different domestic rate, commonly 12.8%, subject to applicable rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Determine the recipient's tax residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, subject-to-tax status and treaty eligibility before payment. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and collect any prescribed treaty-relief form or self-certification. Apply the reduced treaty rate at source only where French procedural requirements and documentation are satisfied; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund where permitted. Retain board resolutions, dividend vouchers, ownership records, residence certificates, beneficial-owner evidence, anti-abuse analysis and proof of remittance. Treaty relief may be denied under principal-purpose, beneficial-ownership, anti-conduit or domestic anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents may be subject to a domestic withholding rate generally of 25%, subject to treaty reduction or exemption. Payments to associated EU companies may qualify for the EU Interest and Royalties Directive exemption if ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax and beneficial-owner conditions are met. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, but exceptions apply, including certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or territories and specific categories of instruments. Treaty rates vary by recipient state and treaty article; apply the lower treaty rate only after confirming residence, beneficial ownership, entitlement and anti-abuse conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer-pricing documentation is generally mandatory for a French entity or French permanent establishment where annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets are at least EUR 400 million, or where the entity is controlled by or controls an entity meeting the EUR 400 million threshold, subject to statutory scope rules. A simplified annual transfer-pricing declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies from EUR 50 million of annual turnover or gross assets, or where the relevant group relationship meets statutory conditions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the selected method is the most appropriate for the transaction and supported by reliable comparables
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single generally applicable economic-substance regulation equivalent to a standalone ESR regime for all companies. Substance is enforced through transfer-pricing rules, permanent-establishment principles, beneficial-ownership requirements, the abuse-of-law doctrine, general anti-abuse rules, anti-hybrid rules, controlled-foreign-company rules, interest limitation rules, withholding-tax anti-conduit principles and principal-purpose testing under treaties. The SAS should maintain French management authority, decision-making evidence, qualified personnel, premises, operational systems, vessel-management functions, risk control, insurance, banking records and commercially supportable contracts. Mere registered-office, nominee-director, back-to-back financing or conduit arrangements are high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing charter revenue, fabricating invoices, understating vessel utilization, falsely deducting personal or shareholder expenses, maintaining parallel accounts, or knowingly filing materially false corporate tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest and penalties up to 80% in aggravated cases. Tax fraud may be punished by up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, with aggravated cases potentially carrying up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3 million fine, subject to the facts and statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers who personally participate, authorize or facilitate the fraud may incur criminal liability, tax-manager liability, civil restitution, director disqualification and asset seizure. Travel restrictions or detention may arise through criminal procedure; piercing of the corporate veil is fact-dependent and not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length charter fees, management fees, royalties, guarantees or interest to foreign related parties; allocating French functions and risks offshore without evidence; or failing to document vessel valuation and beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable income adjustment, withholding tax, late-payment interest, penalties for intentional or fraudulent conduct, documentation penalties and possible denial of deductions or treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for breach of management duties and criminal exposure where fabricated documentation, deliberate tax fraud or money laundering is established. Ordinary transfer-pricing errors do not automatically create personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Conduit and Beneficial-Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French SAS with no real management, personnel, operational control or commercial risk to route dividends, interest, royalties or vessel payments to an undisclosed beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, withholding-tax reassessment, abuse-of-law penalties, corporate tax reassessment, interest, possible beneficial-ownership and anti-money-laundering sanctions, and potential criminal liability if concealment is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed where they knowingly implement nominee structures, false residence claims or sham transactions. Corporate separateness normally remains effective absent fraud, abuse of rights or commingling.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving unexplained maritime payments, using opaque escrow arrangements, disguising beneficial ownership, processing payments involving sanctioned persons or jurisdictions, or failing to perform customer and counterparty due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated forms potentially carrying up to ten years' imprisonment and a EUR 750,000 fine. Legal-entity fines may be multiplied under French criminal law, with confiscation and regulatory consequences also possible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners and compliance officers may face personal criminal liability for knowing participation, concealment or serious facilitation. Asset freezing, confiscation, professional bans and travel restrictions may accompany prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sanctions, Export-Control and Maritime Counterparty Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Chartering, supplying or servicing vessels for sanctioned persons, prohibited offshore projects, embargoed jurisdictions or restricted dual-use activities; falsifying vessel identity, cargo, port calls or beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative asset freezes, payment blocking, contract invalidation, substantial criminal fines, imprisonment, confiscation and loss of access to banking and maritime services. Exact sanctions depend on the applicable EU and French restrictive measure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted for intentional violations or knowing facilitation. Corporate authorization does not shield a director who approved prohibited transactions or ignored obvious sanctions indicators.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared Permanent Establishment, Place of Effective Management or Payroll
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Managing the offshore fleet, concluding contracts, controlling commercial risks or employing operational personnel from France while reporting profits solely in another country.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French corporate tax, VAT, payroll tax and social-security reassessments, interest, late-filing penalties, permanent-establishment adjustments and possible withholding obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil and, in deliberate concealment cases, criminal exposure. A foreign parent's separate legal personality is not a defense to an unreported French permanent establishment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT, Customs and Maritime Documentation Breaches
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying charter services, failing to evidence commercial vessel qualification, claiming unsupported VAT exemptions, misstating import or export status, or using inaccurate ship, port, crew or cargo records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT and customs reassessments, repayment of improperly claimed exemptions, interest, administrative fines, seizure, suspension of customs privileges and possible criminal customs penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise for intentional customs fraud, false declarations or obstruction. Directors remain responsible for implementing reliable compliance controls and document retention.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without distributable reserves, disguising shareholder withdrawals as charter expenses, repaying related-party debt while insolvent, or continuing operations with knowingly insufficient assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unlawful distributions, shareholder repayment, civil damages, management-liability claims, insolvency proceedings and potential criminal penalties for misuse of corporate assets or bankruptcy-related offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution, contribution to insolvency liabilities, management bans and imprisonment for misuse of corporate assets, fraudulent bankruptcy or deliberate continuation of loss-making operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain reliable French accounting records, destroying vessel logs or contracts, backdating invoices, falsifying board minutes, or obstructing a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax assessment based on estimation, rejection of deductions, accounting penalties, criminal sanctions for false documents or obstruction, and adverse evidentiary presumptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and accountants may be personally liable where they ordered, approved or knowingly used false records. Criminal exposure is separate from the SAS's limited liability.
